## What Is an Employer of Record in Equatorial Guinea


An Employer of Record (EOR) is a third-party company that becomes the legal employer of your workers in a foreign country. You direct the work day-to-day, but the EOR holds the employment contract, runs payroll, handles taxes, and keeps everything compliant with local law. No local entity required on your end.


In Equatorial Guinea, this matters. The country operates under a civil law employment framework, with Spanish as its primary official language and the Central African CFA franc (XAF) as its currency. Foreign companies face real structural complexity here: foreign-ownership restrictions, local registration requirements, and an employment code that governs how workers must be hired and paid. Setting up a legal presence takes time, money, and local expertise most companies simply don't have.


An EOR skips all of that. Bolto engages your Equatorial Guinea workers through its own local legal infrastructure, covering contracts, payroll in XAF, tax compliance, benefits, and onboarding. You can[hire globally without the complexity](https://www.bolto.com/employer-of-record) of setting up a local entity. You stay focused on the work itself, while Bolto handles the legal employer obligations that local law requires.


## Employment Laws and Compliance Requirements in Equatorial Guinea


Equatorial Guinea's labor framework is governed by[Law No. 4/2021](https://clarenceabogados.com/client-alert/new-general-labour-law/) , which replaced the previous labor code and updated rules on contract types, recruitment requirements, and termination procedures. These obligations carry real financial liabilities starting on day one.


Foreign-owned entities may face ownership requirements depending on their sector. For companies operating in the oil and gas industry, Equatorial Guinea requires that local citizens hold at least 35% of shares and that one-third of directors be local nationals. Outside the hydrocarbon sector, the local partner requirement was eliminated in 2018 under Law No. 72/2018 (U.S. State Dept., 2025). Even so, entity setup carries real complexity regardless of sector, and an EOR removes the incorporation burden on your end entirely.

## Cost of Hiring in Equatorial Guinea with an EOR vs. a Local Entity


Setting up a local entity (SARL) in Equatorial Guinea is a meaningful commitment. Under Equatorial Guinea's regulations,[oil and gas companies](https://www.healyconsultants.com/equatorial-guinea-company-registration/setup-llc/) are generally required to meet a 35% local shareholding requirement and have one-third of directors who are local citizens (U.S. State Dept., 2025). Entity registration involves government fees, notarial costs, and can take weeks to months, before you've added local legal retainers, tax registration, or bank account setup.


An EOR sidesteps all of that. There are no incorporation costs, no resident director requirements, and no ownership obligations on your end. ## EOR vs. Local Entity in Equatorial Guinea: Which Is Right for You


For most companies, the math in Equatorial Guinea points clearly toward EOR. For oil and gas companies specifically, local regulations require at least 35% local shareholding and that one-third of directors be local citizens (U.S. State Dept., 2025); outside the hydrocarbon sector, the formal local partner requirement was eliminated in 2018. Combined with a setup timeline measured in months, entity formation rarely makes sense until market presence is well grounded.


### When EOR Is the Right Choice


- Early-stage exploration with one to several hires, where the cost of entity overhead outweighs any benefit. Tech companies in particular may also find our guide to[EOR software for tech startups](https://www.bolto.com/blog/best-eor-softwares-for-tech-startups) useful when comparing platforms.
- No existing legal presence in Equatorial Guinea and compliance uncertainty under Law No. 4/2021
- Short timelines where waiting months for entity registration is not viable
- Markets you may need to exit quickly, since dissolving a local corporate structure carries its own legal process. If you already have workers under a different provider, our guide on[how to change employer of record](https://www.bolto.com/blog/how-to-change-employer-of-record-step-by-step) walks through the steps.


### When a Local Entity Becomes Worth Considering


- Consistent headcount above roughly 10 to 15 employees, where per-employee EOR fees outweigh entity costs
- Equity compensation plans that work better under direct employment
- A long-term commitment, particularly in Equatorial Guinea's energy or natural resources sector, where local presence signals credibility with partners and regulators
